sources.name: Allen Human Reference Atlas - 3D, 2020
sources.attribution_text: Song-Lin Ding, Joshua J. Royall, Susan M. Sunkin, Benjamin A.C. Facer, Phil Lesnar, Amy Bernard, Lydia Ng, Ed S. Lein (2020). "Allen Human Reference Atlas – 3D, 2020," RRID:SCR_017764, version 1.0.0. © 2019 Allen Institute for Brain Science. Ontology: Ding et al. 2016, https://doi.org/10.1002/cne.24080.
sources.delineated_in: one brain's atlas drawn on the ICBM 2009b nonlinear symmetric template

route.note: The annotation grid equals the 2009b symmetric template's header, and the gyral labels sit in grey matter on the symmetric tissue map (0.860) but not on the asymmetric one (0.79). Registered with ANTs SyN from the 2009b symmetric T1 to the declared template; the transform is archived by hash. Evidence independent of what the registration optimises: grey-matter share of gyral labels rises to 0.85 with a spread of 0.004 across three settings, and every seeded fault scores lower. For deep structures the gain is not distinguishable from the spread, so their position reads 'not independently checked'. One hemisphere was drawn; the right side is its mirror. The structure table comes from voxel_count.csv in the CC BY download directory, never from the Allen API.

sources.attribution_text: Pauli WM, Nili AN, Tyszka JM. A high-resolution probabilistic in vivo atlas of human subcortical brain nuclei. Sci Data 2018. https://doi.org/10.1038/sdata.2018.63. CC BY 4.0. State changes.

route.note: The publisher's file is on the declared template's 193 x 229 x 193 grid at 1 mm, and the publisher's log names the fixed image as mni_icbm152_t1_tal_nlin_asym_09c.nii. Shift scan K5 of the publisher's own T1 against the declared template is recorded in the pipeline's evidence file. Both sides share one probability map with no side ids; the pipeline assigns sides at x = 0.

sources.arrives_in: MNI152 1 mm (variant not stated; the FSL grid is inferred from file size)

route.note: Space not established, so nothing ships. The file has the FSL 182 x 218 x 182 grid and its left and right labels are exact mirrors about x = +0.5 mm, but no anatomical test separated the FSL template from the declared one: agreement with CIT168's ventral tegmental area is equally poor in both (Dice 0.16), and the share of label voxels in template CSF is not lower after an FSL-to-2009c transform (0.022) than before it (0.013).

sources.arrives_in: MNI152NLin2009bAsym grid at 0.5 mm (asymmetric by measurement; the publisher does not state it)

route.note: The publisher's own T1 correlates 0.931 with the declared asymmetric template and 0.857 with the symmetric one, 0.754 when mirrored, and zero shift scores highest (shift scan K5, recorded in the pipeline's evidence file). Shapes are meshed on the source's 0.5 mm grid and placed through its affine. How the publisher moved the atlas from its own 990-subject template to this grid is not stated.
